title: Topkey + Conduit Integration: Bill the Full Cost of Every Task
summary: A practical guide for Conduit operators: why task spend goes unbilled, how to check your own books, and how Topkey ties every purchase to its Conduit task.
body_markdown:
A guest messages at 8 p.m.: the kitchen faucet won't stop dripping. Conduit's agent answers, opens a repair task, and dispatches your technician. By morning the faucet is fixed and the guest has an update. On the operations side, the job went exactly right.


On the money side, it may not have. Your technician bought a $64 cartridge on a company card on the way over. That purchase lives in a card feed, and the receipt lives in a camera roll. If nobody connects it back to the task, the owner never pays for it, and you do.


This guide is for operators who run tasks in Conduit and want every dollar spent on those tasks to reach the right owner. We'll cover where the money slips, a quick way to check your own books, a few Conduit habits that help, and how the[Topkey + Conduit integration](https://topkey.io/integrations/conduit) closes the loop.


## What a Task Really Costs


Every billable task has three parts: the labor, the materials, and your markup.


Labor is the part Conduit now handles well. Tasks can carry charge rates and totals for billable work, and you can create owner charges straight from a task and push them to your PMS ([Conduit changelog](https://www.conduit.ai/changelog) ).


Materials are where money slips, because they happen outside the task. A technician grabs a part on a company card. A cleaner restocks supplies on a personal card and asks to be paid back. A plumber sends an invoice two weeks after the job. Each of those costs belongs to a task, but nothing ties it to one.


[Markup](https://topkey.io/features/work-orders-markups) depends on the other two. If a material cost never gets tied to its task, your markup on it never gets billed either.


So the question isn't whether your team is doing the work. Conduit makes sure of that. The question is whether the money spent on the work makes it to the owner statement.


## A Five-Minute Check for Your Own Books


You don't need any new software to see how big this gap is for you. Pull last month's card transactions, contractor bills and reimbursements, then ask three questions:


1.


How many of these purchases can you tie to a specific task?


2.


Of those, how many made it onto an owner statement, with your markup?


3.


For the ones that did, could you show the owner the receipt if they asked?


If your numbers drop at each step, you're not alone. One operator we work with billed about $20,000 in owner charges in a single busy month and estimated that, before tying spend to tasks, about half would have been missed. Even a much smaller gap adds up quickly across a portfolio.


## The Same Repair Task, Two Ways


Here's the faucet task again, with example numbers.


**When the spend isn't tied to the task:** the $64 charge shows up in the card feed with a store name and nothing else. At month-end, someone asks around about which property it was for. The technician doesn't remember, and the receipt is gone. The charge gets coded to overhead. The owner is never billed, and neither is your markup.


**When the spend is tied to the task:** the technician texts a photo of the receipt right after the purchase. Later that day, someone on your team attaches the $64 charge to the Conduit repair task in Topkey. Topkey applies the property's markup (say 10%, for $70.40), and the charge is saved to the PMS as an owner charge. The repair task in Conduit now shows the charge, with a link to the receipt. The owner sees a $70.40 line backed by a receipt and tied to a real repair.


The second version takes a couple of minutes of someone's time. The first one costs you the whole charge.


## Habits in Conduit That Help


A few small habits make task spend much easier to track, whatever tools you use for the money side:


-


**Use a task category for billable repairs.** When billable work is easy to filter, it's easy to check that every one of those tasks has its costs attached.


-


**Ask for the receipt in the checklist.** Conduit checklist items can require a photo before they're marked done, so a "photo of receipt" step on repair tasks means the receipt exists before the task closes.


-


**Decide which system bills what.** If you bill labor through Conduit's charge rates, bill materials through your expense process, and agree on the split so nothing is billed twice or skipped.


## How the Topkey + Conduit Integration Works


Topkey is a financial operating system built for vacation rental managers. It brings card spend, receipts, bills and reimbursements into one place, connected to your PMS and accounting software. The integration links that spend to your Conduit tasks.


1.


**Connect.** Add your Conduit API key and Workspace ID in Topkey. API access is part of Conduit's v3 plan, so contact Conduit support to turn it on first.


2.


**Bring in your listings and tasks.** Click Import Properties and Import Tasks. Your Conduit listings match to the properties in your PMS, and tasks from the last 90 days come in with their property, status, priority, category and due date.


3.


**Attach the spend.** On any card transaction, bill or reimbursement in Topkey, pick the property and the Conduit task it was for. The receipt comes with it.


4.


**Review and save.** Topkey applies your markup for that property. Your team reviews the charge, then saves it to your PMS so it lands on the owner statement.


5.


**See it on the task.** Saving also pushes the charge to the Conduit task, with a link back to the receipt in Topkey, so anyone working the task can see what was spent on it.


A few things to know. If you use a PMS, connect it to Topkey before Conduit so your properties don't get duplicated. Tasks come into Topkey when you click Import Tasks, so pull in the latest before attaching new charges.


## What We've Seen When Tasks and Spend Connect


When operators tie every purchase to the task it was for, the results tend to show up in two places: money recovered and time saved at month-end.


An operator in Michigan recovered about $10,000 a month in missed owner charges during busy season, and cut accounting costs 25% while growing from 60 to 100+ properties. A 55-unit operator in Missouri and Colorado saves 15 to 20 hours a week on financial work and recovers about $2,500 a month on average. An 80+ home operator in Florida cut month-end close from 8 days to 2 once technicians started tying purchases to tasks on the spot.


None of that came from working harder. It came from connecting each purchase to its task when it happened, instead of reconstructing it weeks later.


## Common Questions


### Do I Need a PMS to Use the Integration?


No. If you use a PMS, Topkey saves owner charges to it so they land on owner statements. If you don't, you can save charges to Conduit only.


### Which Conduit Plan Do I Need?


The integration connects through Conduit's API, which is part of Conduit's v3 plan. Contact Conduit support to turn on API access, then add your API key and Workspace ID in Topkey.


### Will Owners Get Billed Twice If I Use Conduit's Charge Rates?


Not if you split the costs. Use Conduit's charge rates for labor and attach materials in Topkey. Topkey bills the purchases you attach to a task, not the task's labor, so the two don't overlap.


## Better Together


Conduit makes sure the work gets done and that labor gets billed. Topkey makes sure the money spent on that work reaches the owner too, with a receipt behind it. Your team keeps working in Conduit, and your owner statements finally reflect the full cost of every task.


If you're already on Topkey, you can connect Conduit today with your API key and Workspace ID. If you're not,[see how Topkey + Conduit work together](https://topkey.io/integrations/conduit) and we'll walk you through it.
